subject.title: feat: cross-gateway sessions_send and sessions_spawn via gateway.peers

question: Should core session tools accept a narrow `gateway.peers` cross-gateway path now, or require the broader federation identity/scope contract before adding cross-gateway messaging?
rationale: The feature solves a real workflow gap, but it changes Gateway trust boundaries, credential routing, session ownership, and message-delivery semantics in core.

options.title: Define federation contract first
options.body: Keep this PR paused and settle peer identity, URL policy, operator scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-history semantics before accepting core cross-gateway routing.

options.title: Sponsor a narrow peer-only repair
options.body: Accept the `gateway.peers` direction but remove raw URL tool routing, fix the spawn contract, and require real multi-gateway proof before merge.

options.title: Defer to external bridges
options.body: Decline core federation for now and document plugin, MCP, or operator-built bridge patterns while leaving the canonical issue open only if a missing core API remains.

recommendation.title: Define federation contract first
recommendation.body: Keep this PR paused and settle peer identity, URL policy, operator scopes, replay/idempotency, and session-history semantics before accepting core cross-gateway routing.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent gateway and session-tool history makes this the strongest available routing owner for the cross-gateway/session seam decision.
